reverie_context default-tier overflow (>~25k tokens / ~68KB) was two stacked causes, not one. (1) Project resolution silently failing → scope:auto fell through to global, so project-shaped writes accumulated in the user's global store rather than .reverie/. (2) Once accumulating in global, write-amplification (same key 4-7× per session) inflated byte count faster than entry count suggested. The 2026-05-05 FA-iOS incident: 5 sessions wrote FA-iOS keys (files.icon_detail_view, context.uikit_canimport_pattern, etc.) with project:null → all landed in global. Default-tier bootstrap grew 16K→28K→48K→56K→61K→65K→68K over 8 days. The [project: NONE — auto-scope writes will fall through to global] banner was visible the whole time but was informational only — agents didn't act on it.

FIXES SHIPPED in v1.14:
- (1) Refuse reverie_set on project:null unless scope is explicit (#99, PR #104).
- (2) Soft warning on 3rd+ same-key write per session within 30 min (#101, PR #108).
- Defense in depth: reverie_context size-budget shedding caps the bootstrap response so even an overgrown store doesn't trigger spill-file fallback (#100, PR #108).

See docs/investigation-bootstrap-overflow-2026-05-05.md + docs/dataset-2026-05-05-findings.md for the original investigation.
